request.spec:

DRAFT (each as the claim form would edit it, writing CLAIM_EDITED); claims in any other status keep
theirs.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Changing a plan's amount now also changes the amount of the claims it generated that are still
DRAFT (each as the claim form would edit it, writing CLAIM_EDITED); claims in any other status keep
theirs.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
When a plan's amount changes, the claims it generated that are still DRAFT now take the new amount, and each one writes a `CLAIM_EDITED` record after `PLAN_CHANGED`. Claims in any other status keep their amount. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed**
- **`plan/ChangePlanAmount.java`**: after saving the change and writing `PLAN_CHANGED`, it goes through the claims the plan made. If the plan puts its claims on another sheet, it looks for them there. Each DRAFT gets the new amount and keeps its own date, note, ref and tags. It is saved and recorded with the same `CLAIM_EDITED` line the claim form writes.
- **`claim/ClaimEdit.java`** (new): the claim form's edit rules, moved out of `ApplyClaim` so the form and the plan change both use the same checks. They had to go in a separate class because OfficeFloor won't start if a step class has more than one public method. `ApplyClaim` now just calls it.
- **`plan/PlanRepository.java`**: new `madeClaims(planId)`, which returns the ids of the claims a plan has made.
- I updated the comment in the `plans/{planId}/amount.POST.yml` endpoint file to describe the new behaviour.

**One decision for you:** the request didn't say what should happen when the claim form would refuse to edit one of the drafts. That happens if its due date is in a closed period, another user has its editor open, it has lines, or its person has retired. I skip that claim: it keeps its old amount and gets no `CLAIM_EDITED`. The plan change and the other drafts still go through. The other option would be to refuse the whole plan change if any draft can't be edited; say if you'd prefer that.

No front-end change was needed, because the claim list shows the new amounts once the sheet is reloaded.
